title: Container Bookings: Customer Rolls Beyond the Free Allowance
content:
How many customer roll fees a Container Bookings booking still owes is worked out from the roll notices and fee entries in its charge history, set against the product's number of free customer rolls.

## Rule

The customer rolls of a booking are its roll notices that name the customer as the cause of the roll. If their number is no greater than the product's free customer rolls, no roll owes a fee. Otherwise the number of rolls owing a fee is the customer-roll count less the free customer rolls. From that figure the customer roll fee entries already on the booking are deducted, and what remains is the number of rolls still owing a fee. If nothing remains, no fee is charged.

The rolls still owing a fee are the booking's most recent customer rolls. On each fee entry the vessel and voyage field shows the sailing that the charged roll took the booking off, reproduced exactly as it appears on that roll's notice. Roll notices naming the carrier as the cause play no part in this count.

## Truth table (hypothetical figures)

| Customer roll notices | Free customer rolls | Customer roll fee entries | Rolls still owing a fee |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| 2 | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| 2 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| 3 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 |

In the fourth row the roll still owing is the latest of the three customer rolls, so its fee entry names the sailing shown on the third roll notice. The allowance values in the table are illustrative and are not taken from any product.
